main.title: The Game Awards
main.subtitle: A shared archive of the work we remember
main.summary: A celebration of game makers, with every category winner from 2014 onward.

cards.heading: What the awards celebrate
cards.text: The Game Awards celebrates the people who make games: designers, artists, writers, performers, composers and the teams around them. Created by Geoff Keighley in 2014, the annual show combines awards with performances, announcements and conversations about the medium.

cards.heading: A changing medium, a shared stage
cards.text: An awards archive is also a record of changing priorities. Categories make room for new ways to play and new kinds of work, from independent production and performance to accessibility and community support. Move through the years to read every category winner, then open the official ceremony beside the list.

main.title: Nuclear Throne
main.subtitle: The end of the world will not wait for another try
main.summary: Nuclear Throne combines top-down gunplay, procedurally generated levels and punishing difficulty in a post-apocalyptic world populated by mutants.

cards.heading: From a game jam to public development
cards.text: Nuclear Throne is Vlambeer's 2015 top-down action roguelike, in which mutants fight through a procedurally generated wasteland towards the throne. Each character has active and passive abilities, and a run combines found weapons with radiation-driven mutations. The game grew from the 2013 Wasteland Kings prototype through more than two years of public development and Early Access, reaching computers, PlayStation 4 and PlayStation Vita in December 2015.

cards.heading: Gunplay, difficulty and Early Access success
cards.text: A mutant carries two weapons, making the next pickup a choice about what to keep. Powerful weapons can demand more ammunition or longer reloads, so their strength comes with practical limits during a fight. Reviewers praised the handling of the shooting and the game's responsiveness, while noting its difficulty. During Early Access, Nuclear Throne passed 100,000 sales and one million dollars in revenue.

cards.heading: Mutations change the possibilities of a run
cards.text: Radiation collected from defeated enemies leads to mutations, chosen from a random selection of four. Their value depends on the character and the current run. Crystal can reflect bullets with a shield, while Melting can detonate corpses; a mutation that changes enemy movement or the force of an attack interacts differently with those powers. The combinations give the player another decision as weapons, enemies and opportunities change.

cards.heading: Community maintenance and a tenth-anniversary update
cards.text: After Vlambeer's closure in 2020 and revival under co-founder Jan Willem Nijman in 2024, the game continued to be maintained by community-modder-turned-developer YellowAfterlife. On its tenth anniversary, December 5, 2025, it received "Update #100", which added a thirteenth character, four-player co-operative play, widescreen support and 60+ fps.

cards.heading: Steam-powered pirates in space
cards.text: SteamWorld Heist is a turn-based tactics shooter video game developed and published by Image & Form. The third game in the SteamWorld series, following SteamWorld Dig, SteamWorld Heist has the player control Captain Piper Faraday, a smuggler and occasional pirate, as she recruits a ragtag team of robots and sets out on a space adventure. The objective of the game is for players to board, loot, and shoot their way through enemy spaceships.

cards.heading: From Nintendo 3DS to other platforms
cards.text: SteamWorld Heist debuted on Nintendo 3DS on December 10, 2015. Computer, PlayStation, Wii U and iOS versions followed in 2016. The Switch Ultimate Edition arrived in December 2017, with later releases on cloud services.

main.title: Tokyo Mirage Sessions ♯FE
main.subtitle: An idol agency guards another Tokyo
main.summary: Tokyo Mirage Sessions ♯FE is Atlus's Wii U role-playing game, first released in Japan on 26 December 2015.

cards.heading: An idol agency guards another Tokyo
cards.text: Tokyo Mirage Sessions ♯FE is Atlus's Wii U role-playing game, first released in Japan on 26 December 2015. Young performers at Fortuna Entertainment confront hostile Mirages that harvest human creative energy. Friendly Mirages drawn from Fire Emblem become their partners, letting the cast move between modern Tokyo and the dangerous Idolaspheres. Shibuya, Harajuku and the entertainment agency provide the everyday setting, while stage performance and supernatural combat become connected expressions of the same characters' growing confidence and abilities.

cards.heading: Turn a weakness into a Session
cards.text: The turn-based battles build around weaknesses and Sessions, in which a successful attack leads allies into a chain of further actions. Choosing the right opening can therefore involve much more than the damage dealt by the first character. The player explores the Idolaspheres for resources and equipment while developing those linked abilities. Outside battle, the Wii U GamePad presents messages through the Topic app and supplies area maps. Communication among the cast remains visible alongside the journey through their ordinary work and their otherworldly responsibilities.

cards.heading: A crossover that finds its own stage
cards.text: Nintendo proposed a crossover between Fire Emblem and Shin Megami Tensei, and Atlus shaped the collaboration into an original story about performers. Avex produced the musical numbers, with Yoshiaki Fujisawa composing the score. Side stories follow the ambitions of playable and supporting characters, tying their development to the entertainment setting. The Western edition arrived in June 2016 with Japanese voices and subtitles; an enhanced Switch version, Encore, followed in 2020. The original Wii U adventure makes the crossover's influences part of a new world rather than a simple meeting of existing casts.

main.title: The Witness
main.subtitle: Learning the island?s puzzle rules
main.summary: The Witness is a 2016 puzzle video game developed and published by Thekla, Inc.

cards.heading: An island of panel and environmental puzzles
cards.text: The Witness is a 2016 puzzle video game developed and published by Thekla, Inc. Inspired by Myst, the game involves the exploration of an open world island filled with natural and human-made structures. The player progresses by solving puzzles, which are based on interactions with grids presented on panels around the island or paths hidden within the environment.

cards.heading: Learning the rules by drawing paths
cards.text: Mechanically, all puzzles in The Witness are solved in the same way: a path is drawn on a grid. For a path to be a solution to a puzzle, it must satisfy a number of rules. The rules are usually simple. For example, in a grid with white and black squares, a path may be required to separate the different kinds of squares. The rules are taught to the player throughout the course of the game by the puzzles themselves, as such, there is no text or dialogue directly explaining a puzzle's rules. While the rules a path must satisfy can differ substantially across the game, at least three rules apply to all puzzles: paths must always begin from a round node, end on a line segment with a rounded end, and avoid self-intersection. As such, many of the puzzles can be classified as mazes.

cards.heading: Walking and path-drawing modes
cards.text: The game has two modes of interaction. The first, a walking mode, allows the player to move around and explore the island. The second, the path-drawing mode, is the one the player uses to attempt to solve puzzles. This mode is distinguished from the former by a white border around the screen. In path-drawing mode, the player's avatar is prevented from moving and instead allows the player to use their controls to trace the path through the puzzle's grid. The mode ends once the player solves the puzzle or cancels the mode. Normally, this mode is activated in front of a panel, moving the player's view directly to the panel to solve it, but it can also be activated at any other time. Nearly all puzzles provide immediate feedback if they have been solved correctly or not through sound effects or visual indication.

cards.heading: Finding puzzle paths in the environment
cards.text: Some puzzles ask the player to look beyond the panel. A tree's branches may supply a clue to a nearby grid, while other paths lie across the landscape itself. Their pieces only join when seen from a particular position. Finding that viewpoint changes an ordinary collection of objects into a line the player can trace. These optional discoveries make perspective part of the puzzle rather than merely the camera's position. An early solution can even lead to an alternate ending, carrying the habit of looking for patterns from the island into a live-action scene.

main.title: Detective Pikachu
main.subtitle: A partner who can explain himself
main.summary: Detective Pikachu is Creatures' Nintendo 3DS adventure about Tim Goodman and a talking Pikachu investigating a series of mysteries. Tim can understand his unusual companion, allowing Pikachu's confidence and opinions to become part of their working relationship. The adventure first appeared in Japan as the shorter Birth of a New Duo in 2016, before the expanded worldwide release in 2018. It approaches the Pokémon world through observation and conversation, giving familiar creatures roles as witnesses, suspects or sources of practical help in cases that need to be understood.

cards.heading: A partner who can explain himself
cards.text: Detective Pikachu is Creatures' Nintendo 3DS adventure about Tim Goodman and a talking Pikachu investigating a series of mysteries. Tim can understand his unusual companion, allowing Pikachu's confidence and opinions to become part of their working relationship. The adventure first appeared in Japan as the shorter Birth of a New Duo in 2016, before the expanded worldwide release in 2018. It approaches the Pokémon world through observation and conversation, giving familiar creatures roles as witnesses, suspects or sources of practical help in cases that need to be understood.

cards.heading: Ask the people and the Pokémon
cards.text: The pair collect information from the characters they meet and inspect the places where an incident has occurred. Tim's search for his missing father supplies a larger reason to follow the clues, while smaller cases give the partnership immediate work. A Pokémon's behaviour can be part of the evidence rather than a signal to begin a battle. That changes the player's attention. Recognising a creature still matters, but the useful question is what it has seen, how it relates to the location and whether its actions explain something about the case.

cards.heading: A mystery built for a double act
cards.text: Pikachu's voice makes the companion more than an expressive presence beside the human lead. He can propose an explanation, react to a clue or reveal part of his own uncertain past. Tim's ability to understand him gives their conversations a private quality inside a world where other people hear something different. The narrative adventure format makes room for those exchanges between investigations. Detective Pikachu finds its identity in a simple change to a familiar relationship: the creature at the player's side can now argue, reason and share the work aloud.

main.title: Shin Megami Tensei IV: Apocalypse
main.subtitle: Atlus · Nintendo 3DS
main.summary: Shin Megami Tensei IV: Apocalypse is Atlus's Nintendo 3DS role-playing adventure set during the events of Shin Megami Tensei IV. Nanashi, a young hunter in Tokyo, is killed and revived through an agreement with the deity Dagda. That bargain brings him into a conflict involving the city, its defenders and powers with their own plans for humanity. The familiar landscape gains a different group of companions and a new perspective. Nanashi's relationships become central to deciding what the life returned to him will mean.

cards.heading: A different survivor in Tokyo
cards.text: Shin Megami Tensei IV: Apocalypse is Atlus's Nintendo 3DS role-playing adventure set during the events of Shin Megami Tensei IV. Nanashi, a young hunter in Tokyo, is killed and revived through an agreement with the deity Dagda. That bargain brings him into a conflict involving the city, its defenders and powers with their own plans for humanity. The familiar landscape gains a different group of companions and a new perspective. Nanashi's relationships become central to deciding what the life returned to him will mean.

cards.heading: A party made through conversation and fusion
cards.text: Demons can be negotiated with and recruited, then fused to create stronger companions with selected inherited skills. Their elemental resistances matter as much as their attacks. The Press Turn system again allows a weakness to produce further actions, giving preparation an immediate effect once a battle begins. Smirk status changes the strength and properties of particular abilities, rewarding attention to the state of a fighter as well as the enemy's defences. A reliable party needs several useful answers when its preferred attack is no longer safe.

cards.heading: Human companions change the exchange
cards.text: Nanashi's human allies provide support alongside the controlled demon party, bringing their own abilities into encounters. The story gives those relationships more room as its competing powers ask him to choose whom to trust. Familiar locations and systems allow Apocalypse to begin from an established world while rearranging its loyalties. Ryota Kozuka's music accompanies the journey. The result is a separate adventure within the earlier game's crisis, where the viewpoint of a younger survivor turns an enormous conflict into decisions about the people beside him.
